audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' said 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade' — a shield Ambessa's passive does not give — and never explained why the stage is graded even.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund; Repudiation is her only shield. What actually decides these levels is that Heroic Swing has to be hooked into terrain and is 18s at rank 1, so the stage is even only while he still has the swing.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now states the terrain requirement and the 18s number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is the one stage the chart gives Akshan, and the 'why' was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank'. It never said what his 6 actually is.
audit.why: Comeuppance is 100s at rank 1 with 2500 range and, in Riot's words, it 'deals damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit'. A minion in the line eats the entire shot. That single fact is the whole counterplay to his level-6 spike and it was absent from every field.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the 100s cooldown and the first-thing-hit rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing was described only as 'his dash + camera swing escape'. The two mechanics that beat it were never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Akshan fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... He can jump off early or gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain.' So it needs a wall to exist at all, and putting your body in the swing arc ends it. Ambessa is melee and wants to be in that arc anyway — she just has to know it works.
audit.corrected: tldr, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now state the terrain requirement and the champion-collision knock-off.

audit.whatIsWrong: Going Rogue was only ever called 'his W revive'. The camouflage half was never mentioned, and neither was Dirty Fighting's shield.
audit.why: Riot's text for Going Rogue: 'Akshan enters camouflage and gains Move Speed... Akshan loses the camouflage quickly while he is not in brush or near terrain' — it is a terrain-hugging vanish, and Ambessa's kit contains no reveal, so Control Wards and a sweeper are the only answer. Dirty Fighting shields him on every third hit from his attacks and abilities against a champion, which is exactly the chip that lands during her combo.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] now names Going Rogue and the terrain-hugging camouflage; wants.foe[2] states the every-third-hit shield; spikes[1].text carries the ward requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned that Public Execution takes the farthest champion in the line.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing.' Fired at a grouped Akshan it throws her past him into whoever is behind, and R costs no energy so she can arrive with nothing left for Q, W or E.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[2].d now states the farthest-target rule under its own 'R into peel' title.

edits.after: Stand in his Heroic Swing arc — a champion collision knocks him off it. Ambessa wins the windows where he has no swing.

edits.before: The R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Akshan's ultimate changes the math too.

notes: Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's own descriptions of both abilities say none of that, so I never told the player W or R grounds a dash or heals her. That matters here: the page must not imply she can ground Heroic Swing. The real answer to the swing is body-blocking it, which is in Riot's own Akshan text. Whether her suppression is beaten by tenacity, Cleanse or QSS is in neither kit file and I made no claim. I also left content whys[4] and mid alone — they are accurate about the revive, they were only incomplete, and the camouflage now lives in wants.foe[1] and spikes[1].
